title: WCAG 2.2
note: Curated PARAPHRASED summaries of WCAG 2.2 Level A/AA success criteria for prototype use. Not the verbatim W3C Recommendation; replace with official text via scripts/ingest_knowledge.py before relying on quotations.

criteria.title: Non-text Content
criteria.content: All non-text content presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. Exceptions include controls (which need a name describing their purpose), time-based media, tests, sensory experiences, CAPTCHA, and pure decoration, formatting or invisible content, which must be implemented so that assistive technology can ignore it (for example an img with empty alt text).

criteria.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.content: For prerecorded audio-only and video-only media, an alternative is provided: a transcript or audio description track as appropriate, unless the media is itself a media alternative for text.

criteria.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.content: Captions are provided for all prerecorded audio content in synchronized media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labeled as such.

criteria.title: Info and Relationships
criteria.content: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text. This covers headings, lists, tables, landmarks, and the association of labels with form controls, which must be exposed in markup and not only through visual styling.

criteria.title: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.content: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.

criteria.title: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.content: The purpose of each input field that collects information about the user can be programmatically determined (for example with the autocomplete attribute) when the field serves a purpose from the defined list of input purposes.

criteria.title: Use of Color
criteria.content: Color is not used as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.

criteria.title: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.content: Text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background. Large-scale text (at least 18 point, or 14 point bold) needs at least 3:1. Incidental text, inactive user interface components, pure decoration and logotypes are exempt.

criteria.title: Resize Text
criteria.content: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized without assistive technology up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.

criteria.title: Reflow
criteria.content: Content can be presented without loss of information or functionality, and without scrolling in two dimensions, at a width of 320 CSS pixels for vertical-scrolling content, except for parts that require two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning.

criteria.title: Non-text Contrast
criteria.content: Visual information required to identify user interface components and states, and graphical objects required to understand content, has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.

criteria.title: Text Spacing
criteria.content: No loss of content or functionality occurs when users override line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing and word spacing to the specified minimum values.

criteria.title: Keyboard
criteria.content: All functionality of the content is operable through a keyboard interface without requiring specific timings for individual keystrokes, except where the underlying function requires path-dependent input.

criteria.title: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.content: If keyboard focus can be moved to a component using a keyboard interface, focus can also be moved away from that component using only a keyboard interface, with the user advised if more than unmodified arrow or tab keys are required.

criteria.title: Timing Adjustable
criteria.content: For each time limit set by the content, the user can turn off, adjust, or extend the limit, with exceptions such as real-time events and essential time limits.

criteria.title: Bypass Blocks
criteria.content: A mechanism is available to bypass blocks of content that are repeated on multiple pages, such as a skip link, headings, or landmark regions like main.

criteria.title: Page Titled
criteria.content: Web pages have titles that describe their topic or purpose.

criteria.title: Focus Order
criteria.content: If a page can be navigated sequentially and the navigation sequences affect meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.

criteria.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.content: The purpose of each link can be determined from the link text alone or from the link text together with its programmatically determined link context, except where the purpose would be ambiguous to users in general.

criteria.title: Headings and Labels
criteria.content: Headings and labels describe the topic or purpose of the content they introduce or the control they label.

criteria.title: Focus Visible
criteria.content: Any keyboard operable user interface has a mode of operation where the keyboard focus indicator is visible.

criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.content: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content such as sticky headers or modals.

criteria.title: Label in Name
criteria.content: For user interface components with labels that include text or images of text, the accessible name contains the text that is presented visually.

criteria.title: Dragging Movements
criteria.content: All functionality that uses a dragging movement for operation can be achieved by a single pointer without dragging, unless dragging is essential.

criteria.title: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.content: The size of the target for pointer inputs is at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, except where spacing, an equivalent control, inline placement, user agent control, or an essential presentation applies.

criteria.title: Language of Page
criteria.content: The default human language of each web page can be programmatically determined, for example through a valid lang attribute on the html element.

criteria.title: Language of Parts
criteria.content: The human language of each passage or phrase in the content can be programmatically determined, except for proper names, technical terms, and words of indeterminate language.

criteria.title: On Input
criteria.content: Changing the setting of any user interface component does not automatically cause a change of context unless the user has been advised of the behavior beforehand.

criteria.title: Error Identification
criteria.content: If an input error is automatically detected, the item in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.

criteria.title: Labels or Instructions
criteria.content: Labels or instructions are provided when content requires user input, so users know what information to enter.

criteria.title: Name, Role, Value
criteria.content: For all user interface components, the name and role can be programmatically determined; states, properties, and values that can be set by the user can be programmatically set; and notification of changes to these items is available to user agents, including assistive technologies. Native controls need an accessible name, and ARIA roles, states and properties must be valid and have valid values and ID references.

criteria.title: Status Messages
criteria.content: Status messages can be programmatically determined through role or properties so they can be presented to users by assistive technologies without receiving focus.
